question.text: How can you determine the position of the points: A, B, and C with respect to circle M ?

answers.answer: Compare the distance from M to each point (MA, MB, MC) with the radius r.
solution: Measure or find MA, MB and MC.
Compare each with the radius r.
If the distance is more than r the point is outside; equal to r, on the circle; less than r, inside.

checks.resolve_answer: Compare the distance from M to each point with the radius r: A is outside since MA > r, B is on the circle since MB = r, C is inside since MC < r.

question.text: What is the relation between (MA, r), (MB , r) and (MC , r) ?

answers.answer: MA > r, MB = r, MC < r
solution: A is outside the circle, so MA > r.
B is on the circle, so MB = r.
C is inside the circle, so MC < r.
Answer: MA > r, MB = r, MC < r.

checks.resolve_answer: MA > r (A outside), MB = r (B on the circle), MC < r (C inside).

question.text: If M circle with radius length = 4 cm and A is a point in its plane, Complete:

checks.resolve_answer: On circle M, because MA = r = 4 cm.

question.text: How many tangents can be drawn to circle M ? First: from a point on the circle. Second: from a point outside the circle.
question.stem: from a point on the circle.

solution: A tangent at a point on the circle is perpendicular to the radius at that point.
Only one line is perpendicular to the radius at that point.
Answer: one tangent.

checks.resolve_answer: 1 (exactly one tangent, perpendicular to the radius at that point)

question.text: How many tangents can be drawn to circle M ? First: from a point on the circle. Second: from a point outside the circle.
question.stem: from a point outside the circle.

solution: From a point outside the circle, two lines can touch the circle, one on each side.
Answer: two tangents.

question.text: What is the relation between the two drawn tangents to the circle from the two end points of any diameter in it ?

solution: Each tangent is perpendicular to the radius (the diameter) at its end point.
So both tangents are perpendicular to the same diameter.
Two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel.
Answer: the two tangents are parallel.

checks.resolve_answer: The two tangents are parallel, because both are perpendicular to the same diameter.

question.text: M and N are two intersecting circles at A and B, segment CD is a diameter in circle M and ray CX is a tangent to the circle M at C where ray CX ∩ ray BA = {E}, line MN ∩ segment AB = {F}. Prove that: m(∠DMN) = m(∠CEB).
question.notes: Solution continues on next page, none printed here.

answers.answer: m(∠DMN) = m(∠CEB), proved using the tangent and the line of centers.
solution: CX is a tangent at C, so CX ⊥ CD, so m(∠ECM) = 90°.
Line MN is the line of centers of the intersecting circles, so MN ⊥ AB at F, so m(∠EFM) = 90°.
In quadrilateral ECMF the angles at C and F are 90°, so m(∠CEF) + m(∠CMF) = 180°.
F is on ray EB, so ∠CEF is ∠CEB; F is on ray MN, so ∠CMF is ∠CMN.
C, M, D are collinear, so m(∠DMN) + m(∠CMN) = 180°.
So m(∠DMN) = 180° − m(∠CMN) = m(∠CEB).

checks.resolve_answer: CE is tangent to circle M at C, so CE ⊥ CD, i.e. the angle between CD and CE is 90°. MN is the line of centres, so MN ⊥ AB at F, hence MN ⊥ EB. Line CD (through M) and line MN meet at M, and line CE and line EB meet at E, with CD ⊥ CE and MN ⊥ EB. Angles whose sides are respectively perpendicular are equal (or in quadrilateral CMFE the angles at C and F are 90°, so ∠CMF + ∠CEF = 180°, and ∠DMN is supplementary to ∠CMF). Hence m(∠DMN) = m(∠CEB).

question.text: In the figure opposite: M and N are two intersecting circles at A, B, MN ∩ AB = {C}, AM = 6 cm, AN = 8 cm and MA ⊥ AN. Find the length of AB.

solution: MA ⊥ AN, so triangle MAN has a right angle at A.
MN² = 6² + 8² = 100, so MN = 10 cm.
The line of centers MN ⊥ AB, so AC ⊥ MN in the right triangle.
AC × MN = AM × AN, so AC × 10 = 6 × 8 = 48 and AC = 4.8 cm.
MN bisects the common chord, so AB = 2 × AC = 9.6 cm.
